records.source: Καὶ ἦλθον εἰς τὸ πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης εἰς τὴν χώραν τῶν Γερασηνῶν.
records.gloss: And they came to the other side of the sea, to the region of the Gerasenes.
pieces: They reached the far side of the lake, the country of the Gerasenes.

L.1: And they came to the other side of the sea, to the region of the Gerasenes.

R.1: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers crossed Lake Galilee to the other side. They came to the land where the Gerasene people lived.

decisions.choice: Gerasenes, as the SBLGNT reads
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ on the name. The earliest Alexandrian and Western witnesses have Gerasenes; many later manuscripts have Gadarenes, the name in Matthew 8:28; some have Gergesenes. Gerasa and Gadara were towns of the Decapolis some distance from the lake, and the name may refer to the wider district rather than the town itself. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the other side of the sea: the eastern shore of the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: The crossing began in 4:35. The eastern shore was mostly Gentile country, which explains the herd of pigs (5:11).

decisions.choice: they came: Jesus and his disciples, who set out in 4:35-36
decisions.reason: The plural carries on from the storm on the lake. From 5:2 Mark follows Jesus alone.

decisions.choice: Jesus and his followers crossed Lake Galilee
alternatives: they came to the other side of the sea
decisions.reason: Readable names who is travelling and which lake it is.

records.heading: A man called Legion

records.source: καὶ ἐξελθόντος αὐτοῦ ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου εὐθὺς ὑπήντησεν αὐτῷ ἐκ τῶν μνημείων ἄνθρωπος ἐν πνεύματι ἀκαθάρτῳ, ὃς τὴν κατοίκησιν εἶχεν ἐν τοῖς μνήμασιν, καὶ οὐδὲ ἁλύσει οὐκέτι οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο αὐτὸν δῆσαι διὰ τὸ αὐτὸν πολλάκις πέδαις καὶ ἁλύσεσι δεδέσθαι καὶ διεσπάσθαι ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ τὰς ἁλύσεις καὶ τὰς πέδας συντετρῖφθαι, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἴσχυεν αὐτὸν δαμάσαι·
records.gloss: And having gone out of him out of the boat, immediately met him out of the tombs a man with a spirit unclean, \v 3 who the dwelling had in the tombs, and not even with a chain no longer anyone was able him to bind, \v 4 because him often with shackles and chains to have been bound, and to have been torn apart by him the chains and the shackles to have been shattered, and no one was strong enough him to subdue.
pieces: As soon as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stepped out of the boat, a man with an unclean spirit came out from the tombs to meet {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
This man lived among the tombs, and nobody could keep him tied up anymore, not even with a chain.
Time and again he had been bound hand and foot with irons and chains, but he had pulled the chains apart and smashed the irons on his feet. No one had the strength to control him.

L.2: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had come out of the boat, immediately a man with an unclean spirit met {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [coming] out of the tombs,
L.3: who had his dwelling among the tombs, and no one was able any longer to bind him, not even with a chain,
L.4: because he had often been bound with shackles and chains, and the chains had been torn apart by him and the shackles shattered, and no one was strong enough to subdue him.

R.2: Jesus got out of the boat. Right away a man came out from the burial caves to meet {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. The man had an evil spirit in him.
R.3: He lived in the burial caves. No one could tie him up anymore, not even with chains.
R.4: People had often put chains on his hands and feet. But he always broke the chains apart and smashed the metal rings on his feet. No one was strong enough to control him.

decisions.choice: the tombs: burial caves cut in the hillside
decisions.reason: Tombs in that region were often caves or rooms cut into rock, where a person could shelter. To live among the dead made a person unclean in Jewish law (Numbers 19:11-16).

decisions.choice: not even with a chain, no longer, no one: a string of negatives for emphasis
alternatives: a weaker statement that binding was hard
decisions.reason: Greek piles up negatives to make the point stronger: nothing at all could hold him any more.

decisions.choice: shackles: fetters for the feet
decisions.reason: The word is used for chains or irons on the feet, set beside chains, which could bind the hands.

decisions.choice: subdue: tame, as one tames a wild animal
decisions.reason: The verb is used for taming animals (James 3:7). The man is pictured as wild and beyond human control.

decisions.choice: burial caves
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of tombs a man could live in.

decisions.choice: the long clause is split into separate sentences
alternatives: one sentence with a chain of infinitives
decisions.reason: Balanced breaks the sentence where the Greek gives the reason, to keep it readable.

records.source: καὶ διὰ παντὸς νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας ἐν τοῖς μνήμασιν καὶ ἐν τοῖς ὄρεσιν ἦν κράζων καὶ κατακόπτων ἑαυτὸν λίθοις.
records.gloss: And constantly night and day in the tombs and in the mountains he was crying out and cutting himself with stones.
pieces: Night and day, without stopping, he would scream among the tombs and on the hills and slash himself with stones.

L.5: And constantly, night and day, among the tombs and in the mountains he was crying out and cutting himself with stones.

R.5: All night and all day he was in the burial caves and in the hills. He kept screaming and cutting himself with sharp stones.

decisions.choice: he was crying out and cutting: an ongoing state
decisions.reason: The verb with participles describes what he kept doing, day after day.

decisions.choice: cutting: gashing, wounding
decisions.reason: The verb means to cut or gash. The spirit drives the man to harm himself.

decisions.choice: the mountains: the hills around the lake
decisions.reason: The word covers hill country as well as high mountains.

records.source: καὶ ἰδὼν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἔδραμεν καὶ προσεκύνησεν αὐτόν, καὶ κράξας φωνῇ μεγάλῃ λέγει· Τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί, Ἰησοῦ υἱὲ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ὑψίστου;
records.gloss: And having seen the Jesus from afar, he ran and bowed down to him, \v 7 and having cried out with a voice loud, he says, What to me and to you, Jesus, Son of the God the Most High?
pieces: When he caught sight of Jesus a long way off, he ran up and threw himself down in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
He gave a loud shriek: "Jesus, Son of the Most High God, what have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to do with me?

L.6: And seeing Jesus from a distance, he ran and bowed down before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}},
L.7: and crying out with a loud voice, he says, "What [is there] to me and to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Jesus, Son of the Most High God?

R.6: The man saw Jesus far away. He ran to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and got down on his knees in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
R.7: He shouted very loudly, "Jesus, Son of the Most High God, why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bothering me?

decisions.choice: bowed down: fell to his knees in homage
decisions.reason: The verb is used for kneeling before a king or a god. Here the spirit is forced to bow before one stronger than itself (3:11), not to trust in him.

decisions.choice: what to me and to you: what do we have in common? leave me alone
decisions.reason: As in 1:24, the phrase keeps someone at a distance and is hostile here.

decisions.choice: Son of the Most High God: the spirit knows who Jesus is
alternatives: a title the man had heard from others
decisions.reason: "Most High" is an old name for the God of Israel (Genesis 14:18-20) used also by non-Jews (Acts 16:17). The unclean spirits know Jesus as the Son of God (1:24; 3:11).

decisions.choice: he says: the present tense of storytelling
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present tense to make them vivid. The same is true of the presents through this chapter.

decisions.choice: said, shouted
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the past tense, which English uses for telling a story.

decisions.choice: why are you bothering me?
alternatives: what to me and to you?
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the idiom.

records.source: ὁρκίζω σε τὸν θεόν, μή με βασανίσῃς.
records.gloss: I adjure you by the God, not me torment.
pieces: I beg {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, with God as witness, do not torture me!"

L.7: I adjure {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} by God, do not torment me!"

R.7: Promise me in God's name that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will not hurt me!"

decisions.choice: I adjure you: I put you under oath
decisions.reason: The verb means to make someone swear by God. It is the language used to drive out spirits, here turned against Jesus.

decisions.choice: torment: punish, torture
decisions.reason: The spirits expect punishment at the judgment (Matthew 8:29). The verb is used for torture and for punishment.

decisions.choice: I beg you, with God as witness (B); Promise me in God's name (R)
decisions.reason: "Adjure" is rare in modern English. Balanced and Readable say what the oath formula means.

records.source: ἔλεγεν γὰρ αὐτῷ· Ἔξελθε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἀκάθαρτον ἐκ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
records.gloss: He was saying for to him, Come out, the spirit the unclean, out of the man.
pieces: This was because Jesus had been telling it, "Unclean spirit, come out of this man!"

L.8: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had been saying to him, "Come out of the man, unclean spirit!"

R.8: The man said this because Jesus was already telling the evil spirit, "Get out of this man, evil spirit!"

decisions.choice: for he had been saying: the reason for the spirit's outcry
decisions.reason: Mark explains afterwards what had already happened. The verb can mean that Jesus had begun to command it, or was commanding it while the spirit cried out.

decisions.choice: the unclean spirit: Jesus speaks to the spirit, not the man
alternatives: the man is told to leave
decisions.reason: The words are addressed to the spirit, which is to leave the man.

decisions.choice: This was because (B); The man said this because (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out what "for" explains.

records.source: καὶ ἐπηρώτα αὐτόν· Τί ὄνομά σοι;
records.gloss: And he was asking him, What name to you?
pieces: Then Jesus asked him, "What is your name?"

L.9: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was asking him, "What [is] your name?"

R.9: Then Jesus asked, "What is your name?"

decisions.choice: him, your: addressed to the man, but the spirit answers
decisions.reason: The reply in 5:9 shows the spirits speaking through him.

decisions.choice: what is your name: knowing a spirit's name was thought to give power over it
decisions.reason: Jesus does not need a name to drive out spirits, but the answer shows how many hold the man.

records.source: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Λεγιὼν ὄνομά μοι, ὅτι πολλοί ἐσμεν·
records.gloss: And he says to him, Legion name to me, because many we are.
pieces: He answered, "My name is Legion, since there are many of us."

L.9: And he says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Legion [is] my name, because we are many."

R.9: He answered, "My name is Legion, because there are so many of us."

decisions.choice: Legion: a Roman army unit of several thousand soldiers
alternatives: a vague word for a crowd
decisions.reason: A Roman legion had about 6,000 soldiers. The name says that a great many spirits hold the man, like an occupying army.

decisions.choice: my name ... we are many: the speaker shifts from one to many
decisions.reason: One voice speaks for many spirits. Mark keeps both singular and plural (5:10, 12).

decisions.choice: answered
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the past tense and leave the pronoun out.

records.source: καὶ παρεκάλει αὐτὸν πολλὰ ἵνα μὴ αὐτὰ ἀποστείλῃ ἔξω τῆς χώρας.
records.gloss: And he was begging him much that not them he would send out of the region.
pieces: He kept pleading with Jesus not to send them away out of that country.

L.10: And he begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} many times not to send them out of the region.

R.10: He begged Jesus again and again, "Do not send us away from this area!"

decisions.choice: them: the spirits, though the man speaks
decisions.reason: The plural refers to the spirits, who speak through one voice.

decisions.choice: out of the region: away from the land where they dwelt
decisions.reason: Mark speaks of the region; Luke 8:31 has the abyss. The spirits want to stay where they are.

decisions.choice: direct speech: Do not send us away from this area!
alternatives: that he would not send them out of the region
decisions.reason: Readable turns the request into direct speech, which is easier to follow.

records.source: ἦν δὲ ἐκεῖ πρὸς τῷ ὄρει ἀγέλη χοίρων μεγάλη βοσκομένη·
records.gloss: There was now there near the mountain a herd of pigs great feeding.
pieces: A large herd of pigs happened to be grazing on the hillside nearby.

L.11: Now there was there near the mountain a great herd of pigs feeding.

R.11: There was a big group of pigs eating on the hill close by.

decisions.choice: a herd of pigs: animals the law of Moses calls unclean
alternatives: farm animals of no special meaning
decisions.reason: Jews did not eat or keep pigs (Leviticus 11:7). A large herd shows that this was Gentile country.

decisions.choice: near the mountain: on the slope of the hill
alternatives: at the foot of a high mountain
decisions.reason: The herd is on the hillside above the lake, from which it rushes down (5:13).

records.source: καὶ παρεκάλεσαν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Πέμψον ἡμᾶς εἰς τοὺς χοίρους, ἵνα εἰς αὐτοὺς εἰσέλθωμεν.
records.gloss: And they begged him saying, Send us into the pigs, so that into them we may enter.
pieces: The spirits pleaded with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Send us over to the pigs. Let us go into them."

L.12: And they begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Send us into the pigs, so that we may enter into them."

R.12: The evil spirits begged Jesus, "Let us go into the pigs! Send us into them!"

decisions.choice: they begged: the spirits, now in the plural
decisions.reason: The subject changes to the many spirits, who are named in 5:13.

decisions.choice: they begged him: without a named subject
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add a subject, "all the demons". The shorter text, which the SBLGNT prints, is found in the earliest witnesses. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the spirits (B); the evil spirits (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject, since "they" could mean the people.

records.source: καὶ ἐπέτρεψεν αὐτοῖς.
records.gloss: And he permitted them.
pieces: He gave them leave.

decisions.choice: he permitted: the spirits can act only with Jesus' leave
decisions.reason: The spirits ask; Jesus decides. Mark shows his authority over them (1:27).

records.source: καὶ ἐξελθόντα τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἀκάθαρτα εἰσῆλθον εἰς τοὺς χοίρους, καὶ ὥρμησεν ἡ ἀγέλη κατὰ τοῦ κρημνοῦ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, ὡς δισχίλιοι, καὶ ἐπνίγοντο ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ.
records.gloss: And having gone out, the spirits the unclean entered into the pigs, and rushed the herd down the steep bank into the sea, about two thousand, and they were drowning in the sea.
pieces: Out came the unclean spirits, and they went into the pigs. The whole herd, about 2,000 animals, stampeded down the steep slope into the lake and drowned there.

L.13: And coming out, the unclean spirits entered into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea, about 2,000 [of them], and they were drowned in the sea.

R.13: The evil spirits left the man and went into the pigs. Then the pigs ran wildly down the steep hill into the lake. There were about 2,000 pigs, and all of them drowned in the water.

decisions.choice: about two thousand: the size of the herd
decisions.reason: The number goes with the herd, and is the only number of animals Mark gives. It shows how many spirits had held the man.

decisions.choice: rushed: charged headlong
decisions.reason: The verb is used for a sudden violent rush.

decisions.choice: the spirits destroy what they enter
alternatives: Jesus wanted the pigs to drown
decisions.reason: What the spirits did to the pigs shows what they were doing to the man. The sea in Mark is also a place of chaos that Jesus rules (4:39-41).

decisions.choice: the lake
decisions.reason: As elsewhere, Balanced and Readable call the Sea of Galilee a lake, which it is.

records.source: Καὶ οἱ βόσκοντες αὐτοὺς ἔφυγον καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν εἰς τὴν πόλιν καὶ εἰς τοὺς ἀγρούς· καὶ ἦλθον ἰδεῖν τί ἐστιν τὸ γεγονός.
records.gloss: And those feeding them fled and reported [it] in the city and in the fields; and they came to see what it is that has happened.
pieces: The men tending the pigs ran off and spread the news in the town and on the farms, and people came out to see what had taken place.

L.14: And those feeding them fled and reported [it] in the city and in the countryside, and [people] came to see what it was that had happened.

R.14: The men who took care of the pigs ran away. They told everyone in the town and on the farms what had happened. So people came out to see for themselves.

decisions.choice: the city and the fields: the town and the farms around it
decisions.reason: The word for city is used for towns of any size. "Fields" means the farmland and villages around.

decisions.choice: they came: the people who heard
decisions.reason: The subject is the people of the town and the countryside.

decisions.choice: told everyone ... what had happened
decisions.reason: Readable says what they reported.

records.source: καὶ ἔρχονται πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν, καὶ θεωροῦσιν τὸν δαιμονιζόμενον καθήμενον ἱματισμένον καὶ σωφρονοῦντα, τὸν ἐσχηκότα τὸν λεγιῶνα, καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν.
records.gloss: And they come to the Jesus and see the one being demon-possessed sitting, clothed and being of sound mind, the one having had the legion, and they were afraid.
pieces: When they reached Jesus, they found the man the demons had held sitting there with clothes on and in his right mind, the very man who had been held by the legion. And they were afraid.

L.15: And they come to Jesus and see the demon-possessed man sitting, clothed and in his right mind, the one who had had the legion, and they were afraid.

R.15: They came to Jesus and saw the man who had had all those demons. He was sitting there with his clothes on, and his mind was clear again. This made the people afraid.

decisions.choice: the demon-possessed man: the one who had been possessed
decisions.reason: Mark keeps the description from before. The next words show that he is free now.

decisions.choice: clothed: he had gone without clothes before
decisions.reason: Mark does not say he was naked, but Luke 8:27 does. Being dressed is a sign of his return to normal life.

decisions.choice: of sound mind: sane, in control of himself
decisions.reason: The verb means to have a sound mind, the opposite of the raving he had shown (5:5).

decisions.choice: they were afraid: fear at a power beyond human control
decisions.reason: As the disciples feared after the storm (4:41), the people fear the one who has such power.

decisions.choice: they got to, they saw; they came, saw
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the past tense for the storytelling present.

records.source: καὶ διηγήσαντο αὐτοῖς οἱ ἰδόντες πῶς ἐγένετο τῷ δαιμονιζομένῳ καὶ περὶ τῶν χοίρων.
records.gloss: And described to them those having seen how it happened to the one being demon-possessed, and concerning the pigs.
pieces: Those who had seen it all told them what had happened to the man with the demons, and about the pigs too.

L.16: And those who had seen [it] described to them how it had happened to the demon-possessed man, and about the pigs.

R.16: The people who had seen everything told the others what had happened to the man. They also told them about the pigs.

decisions.choice: those who had seen: the herdsmen and other witnesses
decisions.reason: Mark does not say who they were, only that they had seen it.

decisions.choice: and about the pigs: the loss of the herd is part of the report
decisions.reason: The people hear of both the man's cure and their loss, which leads to their request (5:17).

records.source: καὶ ἤρξαντο παρακαλεῖν αὐτὸν ἀπελθεῖν ἀπὸ τῶν ὁρίων αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: And they began to beg him to depart from the region of them.
pieces: Then they started pleading with Jesus to go away from their district.

L.17: And they began to beg {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to depart from their region.

R.17: Then the people begged Jesus to leave their land.

decisions.choice: they began to beg: the people of the region
decisions.reason: Those who came out to see now ask Jesus to leave.

decisions.choice: to depart from their region: they would rather lose Jesus than face his power
alternatives: they were only angry about the pigs
decisions.reason: Mark gives no reason. Their fear (5:15) and their loss (5:16) are both in view.

records.source: καὶ ἐμβαίνοντος αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ πλοῖον παρεκάλει αὐτὸν ὁ δαιμονισθεὶς ἵνα μετ’ αὐτοῦ ᾖ.
records.gloss: And getting in of him into the boat, was begging him the one having been demon-possessed that with him he might be.
pieces: As Jesus stepped into the boat, the man freed from the demons pleaded to go along with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.18: And as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was getting into the boat, the man who had been demon-possessed was begging {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} that he might be with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.18: Jesus was stepping into the boat. Then the man who used to have the demons begged Jesus, "Please let me go with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!"

decisions.choice: that he might be with him: to go with Jesus as a disciple
decisions.reason: "To be with him" is the phrase Mark used for the Twelve (3:14). The man asks to join those who follow Jesus.

decisions.choice: direct speech: Please let me go with you!
alternatives: that he might be with him
decisions.reason: Readable turns the request into direct speech.

records.source: καὶ οὐκ ἀφῆκεν αὐτόν, ἀλλὰ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ὕπαγε εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου πρὸς τοὺς σούς, καὶ ἀπάγγειλον αὐτοῖς ὅσα ὁ κύριός σοι πεποίηκεν καὶ ἠλέησέν σε.
records.gloss: And not he permitted him, but he says to him, Go to the home of you, to the your own, and report to them how much the Lord for you has done, and had mercy on you.
pieces: But Jesus would not let him, and told him instead, "Go home to your own people, and let them know all that the Lord has done for you, and the mercy {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has shown you."

L.19: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not permit him, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to him, "Go to your home, to your own [people], and report to them how much the Lord has done for you, and [how] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had mercy on you."

R.19: But Jesus did not let him come. Jesus told him, "Go home to your family. Tell them all that the Lord has done for you. Tell them how kind {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has been to you."

decisions.choice: the Lord: God
decisions.reason: Jesus points to God as the one who has acted. In 5:20 the man tells what Jesus did: in Jesus, God has acted.

decisions.choice: go and report: here Jesus sends the man to tell
alternatives: Jesus breaks his own rule of silence
decisions.reason: Elsewhere Jesus forbids people to tell (1:44; 5:43). In Gentile country, away from the crowds of Galilee, he sends this man home to tell what God has done.

decisions.choice: your own: your family and people
decisions.reason: The phrase means those who belong to him: his household and relatives.

decisions.choice: had mercy: showed pity and acted to help
decisions.reason: The verb is used for the pity that moves someone to help (10:47-48).

decisions.choice: how kind he has been to you
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plainer phrase for mercy.

records.source: καὶ ἀπῆλθεν καὶ ἤρξατο κηρύσσειν ἐν τῇ Δεκαπόλει ὅσα ἐποίησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ πάντες ἐθαύμαζον.
records.gloss: And he departed and began to proclaim in the Decapolis how much did for him the Jesus, and all were marveling.
pieces: So he went off and started to tell all through the Decapolis the great things Jesus had done for him. Everyone who heard was astonished.

L.20: And he went away and began to proclaim in the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him, and everyone was amazed.

R.20: So the man left. He went through the area called the Ten Towns, the Decapolis, and told people how much Jesus had done for him. Everyone was amazed.

decisions.choice: the Decapolis: a league of ten Greek cities, mostly east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: The name means Ten Cities. They were Gentile cities of Greek culture, including Gerasa and Gadara.

decisions.choice: proclaim: announce publicly
decisions.reason: Mark uses the same verb for John, Jesus and the disciples (1:4, 14; 3:14). The healed man becomes a herald.

decisions.choice: how much Jesus had done: told to report what the Lord did (5:19), he tells what Jesus did
decisions.reason: Mark sets "the Lord" in 5:19 beside "Jesus" here without comment. The reader is left to see that God's work is done through Jesus.

decisions.choice: the area called the Ten Towns, the Decapolis
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name.

records.source: Καὶ διαπεράσαντος τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ πάλιν εἰς τὸ πέραν συνήχθη ὄχλος πολὺς ἐπ’ αὐτόν, καὶ ἦν παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν.
records.gloss: And having crossed over the Jesus in the boat again to the other side, was gathered a crowd great to him, and he was beside the sea.
pieces: When Jesus had gone back across by boat, a large crowd gathered around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was still by the lake.

L.21: And when Jesus had crossed over again in the boat to the other side, a great crowd gathered around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was beside the sea.

R.21: Jesus went back across Lake Galilee in the boat. A big crowd came together around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stood on the shore.

decisions.choice: to the other side: back to the western, Jewish shore
decisions.reason: Jesus returns to Galilee, where the crowds wait for him (4:1).

decisions.choice: in the boat, as the SBLGNT reads
decisions.reason: A few early manuscripts lack "in the boat". The sense is the same either way. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: on the shore
decisions.reason: Readable calls the lakeside the shore.

records.heading: Jairus pleads for his daughter

records.source: καὶ ἔρχεται εἷς τῶν ἀρχισυναγώγων, ὀνόματι Ἰάϊρος, καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὸν πίπτει πρὸς τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ παρακαλεῖ αὐτὸν πολλὰ λέγων ὅτι Τὸ θυγάτριόν μου ἐσχάτως ἔχει, ἵνα ἐλθὼν ἐπιθῇς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῇ ἵνα σωθῇ καὶ ζήσῃ.
records.gloss: And comes one of the synagogue leaders, by name Jairus, and having seen him falls at the feet of him \v 23 and begs him much saying that, The little daughter of me at the end is holding, that having come you would lay the hands on her so that she may be saved and live.
pieces: One of the leaders of the synagogue, a man named Jairus, came up. When he saw Jesus, he threw himself at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet
and pleaded with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} again and again. "My little daughter is dying," he said. "Please come and put {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hands on her, so that she may get well and live."

L.22: And one of the synagogue leaders, Jairus by name, comes, and seeing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} he falls at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet
L.23: and begs {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} earnestly, saying, "My little daughter is at the point of death. [I beg {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}] that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come and lay [{{deity_pronoun:your|Your}}] hands on her, so that she may be saved and live."

R.22: A man named Jairus came. He was one of the leaders of the local synagogue. When Jairus saw Jesus, he bowed down at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet.
R.23: He begged Jesus over and over, "My little girl is about to die. Please come and put {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hands on her. Then she will get well and live!"

decisions.choice: synagogue leader: the man in charge of the synagogue's meetings
decisions.reason: A synagogue leader arranged worship and chose who would read and teach. He was a respected man in the town.

decisions.choice: is holding at the end: is at the point of death
decisions.reason: The phrase means near the end of life. She is still alive (5:35).

decisions.choice: be saved: be made well, rescued from death
decisions.reason: The verb is used both for healing and for God's saving. Here it means rescued from her illness, set beside "live"; the wider sense may be heard too.

decisions.choice: that you would come and lay: an urgent request without a main verb
decisions.reason: The clause stands on its own as a plea. "I beg you" is understood.

decisions.choice: lay hands on her: touch to heal and bless
decisions.reason: Laying on of hands was a sign of blessing and was expected from a healer (6:5; 8:23).

decisions.choice: get well
decisions.reason: In a request for a sick child, Balanced and Readable use the healing sense. Literal keeps the word that can also mean salvation.

decisions.choice: one of the leaders of the local synagogue
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that he led a local meeting place.

records.source: καὶ ἀπῆλθεν μετ’ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And he went with him.
pieces: So Jesus set out with him.

decisions.choice: him: Jairus
decisions.reason: Jesus goes with the father to his house.

records.source: Καὶ ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ ὄχλος πολύς, καὶ συνέθλιβον αὐτόν.
records.gloss: And was following him a crowd great, and were pressing around him.
pieces: A huge crowd went along behind {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, jostling {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on every side.

L.24: And a great crowd was following {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and they were pressing around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.24: A big crowd followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. People were pushing against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from all sides.

decisions.choice: pressing around: crushing in on him
decisions.reason: The verb means to press hard from all sides. It explains the disciples' answer in 5:31.

records.heading: Twelve years of bleeding

records.source: καὶ γυνὴ οὖσα ἐν ῥύσει αἵματος δώδεκα ἔτη καὶ πολλὰ παθοῦσα ὑπὸ πολλῶν ἰατρῶν καὶ δαπανήσασα τὰ παρ’ αὐτῆς πάντα καὶ μηδὲν ὠφεληθεῖσα ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον εἰς τὸ χεῖρον ἐλθοῦσα, ἀκούσασα περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, ἐλθοῦσα ἐν τῷ ὄχλῳ ὄπισθεν ἥψατο τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ·
records.gloss: And a woman being with a flow of blood twelve years \v 26 and many [things] having suffered under many physicians and having spent the from her all and nothing having benefited but rather to the worse having come, \v 27 having heard concerning the Jesus, having come in the crowd behind, touched the garment of him.
pieces: In the crowd was a woman who had been bleeding for twelve years.
She had gone through a great deal at the hands of many doctors and had spent everything she owned. Instead of getting better, she had only grown worse.
She had heard about Jesus, so she made her way through the crowd and touched {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} cloak from behind.

L.25: And a woman who had had a flow of blood [for] twelve years,
L.26: and had suffered much under many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and had not benefited at all but rather had grown worse,
L.27: having heard about Jesus, came up in the crowd behind [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] and touched {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} garment.

R.25: A woman was there who had been sick with bleeding for twelve years.
R.26: Many doctors had tried to help her, and they had caused her a lot of pain. She had spent all her money on them. But she was not getting better. She was getting worse.
R.27: This woman had heard about Jesus. So she pushed through the crowd and touched {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} coat from behind.

decisions.choice: a flow of blood: continual bleeding, most likely from the womb
decisions.reason: The phrase is the one used in Leviticus 15:25 for a woman's bleeding outside her monthly period.

decisions.choice: a flow of blood: in the law of Moses it made her unclean
decisions.reason: Under Leviticus 15:25-27 she was unclean all those years, and so was anything she touched. That is why she came from behind in secret.

decisions.choice: one long sentence of participles leading to she touched
decisions.reason: Mark piles up seven participles describing her story before the one main verb, touched.

decisions.choice: suffered much under many physicians: the treatments themselves hurt her
decisions.reason: Medicine of the time could be painful. Mark notes that it cost her everything and did no good.

decisions.choice: garment: the outer cloak
decisions.reason: The word is used for the outer robe. Matthew 9:20 and Luke 8:44 say she touched its fringe.

decisions.choice: the sentence is broken into several
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break the chain of participles into separate sentences.

decisions.choice: Many doctors had tried to help her, and they had caused her a lot of pain
alternatives: had suffered much under many physicians
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what suffering under doctors meant.

records.source: ἔλεγεν γὰρ ὅτι Ἐὰν ἅψωμαι κἂν τῶν ἱματίων αὐτοῦ σωθήσομαι.
records.gloss: She was saying for that, If I touch even the garments of him, I will be saved.
pieces: She kept telling herself, "Even if all I touch is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothes, I will be made well."

L.28: For she was saying, "If I touch even {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} garments, I will be saved."

R.28: She thought, "If I can only touch {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothes, I will get well."

decisions.choice: she was saying: saying to herself
decisions.reason: The verb is continuous: she kept saying this, most likely to herself.

decisions.choice: I will be saved: I will be made well
decisions.reason: As in 5:23, the verb means rescue from her illness; Jesus' reply in 5:34 uses the same verb and lets its wider sense be heard.

decisions.choice: even: even his clothes, if not himself
decisions.reason: The word means "even" or "if only". She dares not ask him directly.

decisions.choice: be made well (B); get well (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the healing sense, which is what she has in mind.

records.source: καὶ εὐθὺς ἐξηράνθη ἡ πηγὴ τοῦ αἵματος αὐτῆς, καὶ ἔγνω τῷ σώματι ὅτι ἴαται ἀπὸ τῆς μάστιγος.
records.gloss: And immediately was dried up the source of the blood of her, and she knew in the body that she has been healed from the affliction.
pieces: At once her bleeding stopped, and she could feel in her body that she was free of her suffering.

L.29: And immediately the source of her blood was dried up, and she knew in [her] body that she had been healed of the affliction.

R.29: Right away her bleeding stopped. She could feel in her body that she was healed.

decisions.choice: source: the place the bleeding came from
decisions.reason: The word means a spring or fountain. Leviticus 12:7 uses it for a woman's bleeding.

decisions.choice: affliction: a disease, literally a whip or scourge
decisions.reason: The word means a whip, and was used for a painful illness (3:10). It does not say the illness was a punishment.

decisions.choice: she knew: she could feel it
decisions.reason: She is certain from what she feels in her body.

records.source: καὶ εὐθὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐπιγνοὺς ἐν ἑαυτῷ τὴν ἐξ αὐτοῦ δύναμιν ἐξελθοῦσαν ἐπιστραφεὶς ἐν τῷ ὄχλῳ ἔλεγεν· Τίς μου ἥψατο τῶν ἱματίων;
records.gloss: And immediately the Jesus having known in himself the out of him power having gone out, having turned around in the crowd he was saying, Who of me touched the garments?
pieces: Right away Jesus knew within {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} that power had gone out of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He turned around in the crowd and said, "Who touched {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} clothes?"

L.30: And immediately Jesus, knowing in {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} that power had gone out from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, turned around in the crowd and was saying, "Who touched {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} garments?"

R.30: At that moment Jesus knew that power had gone out from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} turned to face the people and asked, "Who touched {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} clothes?"

decisions.choice: power: the power to heal
decisions.reason: The word is the one Mark uses for miracles (6:2, 5). Healing power went out from Jesus.

decisions.choice: knowing in himself: he was aware of it within
decisions.reason: Jesus knew at once, without being told.

decisions.choice: who touched my garments: Jesus asks in order to meet her
alternatives: Jesus did not know who it was
decisions.reason: Mark does not explain whether Jesus knew. His question brings the woman forward to be seen and spoken to (5:33-34).

records.source: καὶ ἔλεγον αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ· Βλέπεις τὸν ὄχλον συνθλίβοντά σε, καὶ λέγεις· Τίς μου ἥψατο;
records.gloss: And were saying to him the disciples of him, You see the crowd pressing around you, and you say, Who of me touched?
pieces: His disciples said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "You can see how the crowd is crushing in on {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. How can {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} ask, 'Who touched {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?'"

L.31: And {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples were saying to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "You see the crowd pressing around {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} say, 'Who touched {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?'"

R.31: His followers said, "Look at all these people pushing against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}! How can {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} ask, 'Who touched {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?'"

decisions.choice: you see ... and you say: a reproachful question
decisions.reason: The disciples think the question makes no sense with so many people touching him.

decisions.choice: How can you ask
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the disciples' surprise plain.

records.source: καὶ περιεβλέπετο ἰδεῖν τὴν τοῦτο ποιήσασαν.
records.gloss: And he was looking around to see the one this having done.
pieces: But Jesus went on searching the faces around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for the one who had done it.

L.32: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was looking around to see the [woman] who had done this.

R.32: But Jesus kept looking at the people around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to find out who had touched {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: the one who had done this: the participle is feminine
alternatives: Jesus knew she was a woman
decisions.reason: The Greek form is feminine. Mark the narrator knows it was a woman; it does not say whether Jesus did.

decisions.choice: was looking around: he kept looking
decisions.reason: The verb is continuous: he did not give up searching.

decisions.choice: [woman]
decisions.reason: Literal shows the feminine form with a bracketed word.

records.source: ἡ δὲ γυνὴ φοβηθεῖσα καὶ τρέμουσα, εἰδυῖα ὃ γέγονεν αὐτῇ, ἦλθεν καὶ προσέπεσεν αὐτῷ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ πᾶσαν τὴν ἀλήθειαν.
records.gloss: The and woman, having been afraid and trembling, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell down before him and told him all the truth.
pieces: Then the woman, afraid and shaking, knowing what had been done for her, came forward, dropped down before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the whole truth.

L.33: And the woman, frightened and trembling, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell down before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the whole truth.

R.33: The woman knew what had happened to her. She was afraid and shaking. She came and bowed down in front of Jesus. Then she told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the whole truth.

decisions.choice: frightened and trembling: awe as well as fear
decisions.reason: She may have feared blame for touching him while unclean. The same words are used for awe before God's power.

decisions.choice: the whole truth: everything that had happened
decisions.reason: She tells her whole story openly, before the crowd.

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Θυγάτηρ, ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε· ὕπαγε εἰς εἰρήνην, καὶ ἴσθι ὑγιὴς ἀπὸ τῆς μάστιγός σου.
records.gloss: He and said to her, Daughter, the faith of you has saved you; go in peace, and be healthy from the affliction of you.
pieces: "Daughter," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told her, "your faith has saved you and made you well. Go in peace, free of your suffering."

L.34: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to her, "Daughter, your faith has saved you. Go in peace, and be healthy, [free] from your affliction."

R.34: Jesus said to her, "My daughter, your faith has made you well and saved you. Go in peace. Your sickness is gone for good."

decisions.choice: has saved: has made well, and more
decisions.reason: The verb is the one she used in 5:28, which means both healing and rescue by God. Her body is healed already (5:29); Jesus' words also give her a place restored before God and the people.

decisions.choice: faith: trust in Jesus to heal
decisions.reason: Her faith is shown in what she did: reaching out to Jesus. Jesus credits her faith, not her touch or the cloak.

decisions.choice: go in peace: a farewell and blessing
decisions.reason: The words are a common Jewish farewell (1 Samuel 1:17). Peace means wholeness and well-being.

decisions.choice: daughter: a word of warmth and of welcome
decisions.reason: Jesus calls the unclean woman "daughter", taking her into the family of God's people (3:35).

decisions.choice: be healthy from your affliction: stay healed
decisions.reason: Jesus confirms that the cure is real and lasting.

decisions.choice: saved you and made you well (B); made you well and saved you (R)
decisions.reason: One English verb cannot carry both senses, so Balanced and Readable use two. Literal keeps the single verb.

records.source: Ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἔρχονται ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀρχισυναγώγου λέγοντες ὅτι Ἡ θυγάτηρ σου ἀπέθανεν· τί ἔτι σκύλλεις τὸν διδάσκαλον;
records.gloss: Still him speaking, they come from the synagogue leader saying that, The daughter of you died; why still trouble the teacher?
pieces: While Jesus was still talking, some people arrived from the synagogue leader's house. "Your daughter is dead," they said. "There is no need to bother the teacher any more."

L.35: While {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was still speaking, they come from the [house of the] synagogue leader, saying, "Your daughter has died. Why trouble the teacher any longer?"

R.35: Jesus was still speaking when some people came from Jairus's house. They said to Jairus, "Your daughter has died. Do not make the teacher come now."

decisions.choice: from the synagogue leader: from his house
decisions.reason: Jairus is with Jesus, so the messengers come from his household.

decisions.choice: why trouble the teacher any longer: it is too late
decisions.reason: The question means there is no point now. They expect nothing more.

decisions.choice: they come: the present tense of storytelling
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in the chapter.

decisions.choice: They said to Jairus
decisions.reason: Readable names the one they speak to.

records.heading: Little girl, get up

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς παρακούσας τὸν λόγον λαλούμενον λέγει τῷ ἀρχισυναγώγῳ· Μὴ φοβοῦ, μόνον πίστευε.
records.gloss: The but Jesus, having overheard the word being spoken, says to the synagogue leader, Not fear, only believe.
pieces: But Jesus paid no attention to what they said and told the synagogue leader, "Do not be afraid. Just believe."

L.36: But Jesus, overhearing the word being spoken, says to the synagogue leader, "Do not fear, only believe."

R.36: Jesus heard what they said, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} paid no attention to it. He told Jairus, "Do not be afraid. Only believe."

decisions.choice: overhearing: hearing and ignoring
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to overhear or to take no notice. Both fit: Jesus heard the message and set it aside.

decisions.choice: do not fear, only believe: keep on believing
decisions.reason: Both verbs are present commands: stop fearing, keep on believing. Fear is the opposite of faith in Mark (4:40).

decisions.choice: believe: trust Jesus even in the face of death
decisions.reason: Jairus is called to the same trust the woman showed (5:34).

decisions.choice: paid no attention to
decisions.reason: Balanced takes the sense of ignoring; Readable shows both. The footnote gives the other sense.

records.source: καὶ οὐκ ἀφῆκεν οὐδένα μετ’ αὐτοῦ συνακολουθῆσαι εἰ μὴ τὸν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν ἀδελφὸν Ἰακώβου.
records.gloss: And not he permitted anyone with him to follow except the Peter and James and John the brother of James.
pieces: He would not let anyone come with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} except Peter, James, and James's brother John.

L.37: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not permit anyone to follow along with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} except Peter and James and John the brother of James.

R.37: Jesus let only Peter, James, and John go with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. John was James's brother.

decisions.choice: Peter, James and John: the inner group of disciples
decisions.reason: These three also see the transfiguration (9:2) and are near Jesus in Gethsemane (14:33).

records.source: καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ ἀρχισυναγώγου, καὶ θεωρεῖ θόρυβον καὶ κλαίοντας καὶ ἀλαλάζοντας πολλά, καὶ εἰσελθὼν λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τί θορυβεῖσθε καὶ κλαίετε;
records.gloss: And they come to the house of the synagogue leader, and he sees a commotion and weeping and wailing much, \v 39 and having gone in he says to them, Why are you making commotion and weeping?
pieces: When they reached the synagogue leader's house, Jesus saw an uproar, with people crying and howling in grief.
He went in and asked them, "Why all this noise and crying?

L.38: And they come to the house of the synagogue leader, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sees a commotion, and [people] weeping and wailing loudly,
L.39: and going in, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "Why are you making a commotion and weeping?

R.38: They came to the house of Jairus. Jesus saw that there was a lot of noise and confusion. People were crying loudly. Some were wailing for the dead girl.
R.39: Jesus went inside and said to them, "Why are you making all this noise? Why are you crying?

decisions.choice: commotion, weeping and wailing: the loud mourning that followed a death
decisions.reason: Mourning began at once and was loud. Families hired flute players and mourning women (Matthew 9:23; Jeremiah 9:17).

decisions.choice: he sees: the present tense of storytelling
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in the chapter, Mark tells the story in the present tense.

decisions.choice: reached, saw, asked; came, saw, said
alternatives: they come, he sees, he says
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the past tense.

decisions.choice: Some were wailing for the dead girl
decisions.reason: Readable says why they were wailing.

records.source: τὸ παιδίον οὐκ ἀπέθανεν ἀλλὰ καθεύδει.
records.gloss: The child not died but sleeps.
pieces: The child is not dead. She is asleep."

L.39: The child has not died but is sleeping."

R.39: The girl is not dead. She is only sleeping."

decisions.choice: sleeps: her death will be like a sleep from which she wakes
decisions.reason: The messengers and mourners know she has died (5:35, 40). Jesus speaks of death as a sleep that he will end, as in John 11:11-14.

decisions.choice: the girl
decisions.reason: Readable names her as a girl, as 5:41 does.

records.source: καὶ κατεγέλων αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And they were laughing at him.
pieces: They laughed at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: laughing at: mocking with scorn
decisions.reason: The verb means to laugh someone down. They know she is dead.

records.source: αὐτὸς δὲ ἐκβαλὼν πάντας παραλαμβάνει τὸν πατέρα τοῦ παιδίου καὶ τὴν μητέρα καὶ τοὺς μετ’ αὐτοῦ, καὶ εἰσπορεύεται ὅπου ἦν τὸ παιδίον·
records.gloss: He but having put out all takes the father of the child and the mother and those with him, and goes in where was the child.
pieces: But Jesus sent them all outside. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the disciples who were with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and the child's father and mother, and went into the room where the girl lay.

L.40: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, putting them all out, takes the child's father and mother and those with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and goes in where the child was.

R.40: But Jesus made all the people go outside. He took the girl's father and mother and the three followers who were with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They went into the room where the girl was lying.

decisions.choice: putting out: sending out firmly
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for driving out spirits, but here it means to make people leave.

decisions.choice: those with him: Peter, James and John (5:37)
decisions.reason: Only these three disciples came with him to the house.

decisions.choice: the disciples (B); the three followers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who they were, from 5:37.

records.source: καὶ κρατήσας τῆς χειρὸς τοῦ παιδίου λέγει αὐτῇ· Ταλιθα κουμ, ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον· Τὸ κοράσιον, σοὶ λέγω, ἔγειρε.
records.gloss: And having taken hold of the hand of the child he says to her, Talitha koum, which is being translated, Little girl, to you I say, get up.
pieces: He took the child by the hand and said to her, "Talitha koum," which means, "Little girl, I tell you, get up."

L.41: And taking hold of the child's hand, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to her, "Talitha koum," which is translated, "Little girl, I say to you, get up."

R.41: Jesus took the girl's hand and said to her, "Talitha koum." These words mean, "Little girl, I am telling you to get up!"

decisions.choice: Talitha koum: Aramaic words, kept and translated by Mark
decisions.reason: Aramaic was the everyday language of Jesus and his people. Mark keeps his very words and translates them for Greek readers (7:34; 14:36).

decisions.choice: get up: rise, a word also used for rising from death
decisions.reason: The verb is ordinary, for getting up from bed, but it is also used for being raised from the dead (16:6).

decisions.choice: I say to you: Mark adds these words to the translation
decisions.reason: The Aramaic is only "little girl, get up". The added words stress the authority of Jesus' command.

decisions.choice: Talitha koum, written in English letters
alternatives: little girl, arise, without the Aramaic
decisions.reason: All levels keep the Aramaic words as Mark does, since he translates them himself.

records.source: καὶ εὐθὺς ἀνέστη τὸ κοράσιον καὶ περιεπάτει, ἦν γὰρ ἐτῶν δώδεκα.
records.gloss: And immediately rose up the girl and was walking around; she was for of years twelve.
pieces: At once the girl stood up and walked about, for she was twelve years old.

L.42: And immediately the girl got up and was walking around; for she was twelve years [old].

R.42: Right away the girl stood up and started walking around. She was twelve years old.

decisions.choice: for she was twelve years old: explains why she could walk
alternatives: explains why she was called a little girl
decisions.reason: The "for" explains that she was not a baby but old enough to walk. Her twelve years echo the woman's twelve years of illness (5:25).

decisions.choice: got up: rose
decisions.reason: She rises at Jesus' word. The same verb is used for rising from death (8:31).

records.source: καὶ ἐξέστησαν εὐθὺς ἐκστάσει μεγάλῃ.
records.gloss: And they were amazed immediately with amazement great.
pieces: Everyone was astounded on the spot.

L.42: And immediately they were overcome with great amazement.

R.42: Her parents and the followers were completely amazed.

decisions.choice: amazed with great amazement: utterly astonished
decisions.reason: Greek repeats the root of the verb in the noun to make it stronger. The word means to be beside oneself.

decisions.choice: Her parents and the followers
decisions.reason: Readable names who was in the room (5:40).

records.source: καὶ διεστείλατο αὐτοῖς πολλὰ ἵνα μηδεὶς γνοῖ τοῦτο, καὶ εἶπεν δοθῆναι αὐτῇ φαγεῖν.
records.gloss: And he ordered them much that no one should know this, and he said to be given to her to eat.
pieces: Jesus gave them strict orders not to let anyone find out about this, and said she should be given food.

L.43: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} strictly ordered them that no one should know this, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said [that something] should be given to her to eat.

R.43: Jesus told them firmly, "Do not let anyone know about this." Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them to give her some food.

decisions.choice: no one should know this: Jesus keeps his work hidden
alternatives: he wanted the girl to rest
decisions.reason: As in 1:44 and 3:12, Jesus forbids spreading the news. The mourners outside would soon learn she was alive, but how it happened was to stay with these few.

decisions.choice: to be given to her to eat: a practical command
decisions.reason: She is fully alive and needs food, like anyone else.

decisions.choice: direct speech: Do not let anyone know about this
alternatives: that no one should know this
decisions.reason: Readable turns the order into direct speech.
